The issue is about "evaluating stringified annotations in Python 3.10". This suggests that when an annotation is provided as a string (e.g., `"str"` instead of `str`), the code fails to correctly interpret it as a type object, especially in newer Python versions where type hinting behavior might have changed or where string parsing needs to be more robust.

`fastapi/_compat/shared.py` contains several functions dealing with annotation types (`field_annotation_is_sequence`, `is_bytes_or_nonable_bytes_annotation`, etc.).
